title: Experience Report by 吉原
paragraphs: From October 4 to 6, 2017, I took part in the FAN Symposium (a joint symposium of the University of Freiburg, the University of Adelaide and Nagoya University), held at the University of Freiburg in Germany, and I would like to report on it. The FAN Symposium is held by these three universities to promote exchange at the research level and to explore joint research, and it invites researchers and students from each university. I was invited to participate because I entered the Nagoya University-University of Adelaide International Joint Graduate Program in Medicine last April. Freiburg (officially Freiburg im Breisgau) is located in southwestern Germany and is famous as an environmental city. Water channels run throughout the cathedral and the old town, and many tourists visit the beautiful townscape every year. Freiburg is also well known as a university town. The University of Freiburg (officially Albert-Ludwigs-Universität Freiburg) in the centre of the city is said to be the fifth oldest university in Germany. It has produced many outstanding researchers and, starting with its Faculty of Medicine, is one of the most prestigious universities in Europe. I arrived on October 2. The next day, October 3, was a public holiday in Germany, so I walked around the city while forcing myself to adjust to the time difference. The University of Freiburg is located next to the station. On its large campus stand the Faculty of Medicine, the university hospital and many research buildings, and it had the dignity of an academic city. Beautiful water channels are scattered through the old town, and the cathedral rises majestically in the middle of the city. It is a precious heritage that preserves the grandeur of the Middle Ages, and the surrounding area was lively with restaurants and served as a place of rest for the townspeople. From a small hill in the suburbs, I could take in a view of the vast farmland and pastures and the picturesque hills of Europe. (2 photos) On the 4th and 5th, under the arrangements of Dr. Christoph Peters, I was allowed to visit the laboratory of Professor Thomas Reinheckel. The laboratory mainly carried out experiments using animal models on the theme of the role of proteases in cancer, especially cathepsins. Although they make full use of advanced technologies such as genome editing and omics analysis, research on proteases, a basic and most important group of proteins in biochemistry, is truly a classic theme. It also has a high potential for therapeutic application and a translational side, and I was impressed by the breadth of vision and the accuracy of foresight of the professors, which was a very good stimulus for me. In the future, as with the University of Adelaide, a formal partnership with Nagoya University is planned and a new joint degree program will be established. I hope that candidates from our laboratory will also enter the program and that joint research with the University of Freiburg will be realised. On the 6th, I took part in the FAN Symposium and presented my own research. After the symposium, I attended a reception at a restaurant next to the cathedral. I also had the opportunity to talk with graduate students from the University of Adelaide and obtained firsthand information from the local people. The content was interesting, but above all, what I felt was the difficulty of communicating in English. I could not deny that there were parts of the expressions and attitudes, rooted in the borderless culture of the English-speaking world, that were hard for me to accept, as I have no experience of living abroad for a long period. This is a source of anxiety for my study in Australia starting next January, but seeing my own challenges clearly was a great gain, and I would like to connect it to the motivation to make an effort to overcome them. Overall, it was a trip from which I gained a great deal. I hope to share what I felt and learned in this experience with my peers and to contribute to the development of our laboratory. Finally, I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to the professors of Nagoya University who gave me this opportunity and to the staff of the International Collaboration Office who supported me with the travel procedures. I will continue to do my best. Thank you very much.
